Thin-plate spline surface

Source: R/tpsurf.R
tpsurf.Rd

tpsurf() fits a thin-plate spline to values measured at points in the plane (rates at area centroids, say) and evaluates it on a grid over their box: a smooth surface that passes through the values when lam is 0 and is smoothed towards a plane as lam grows. It complements kdsurf(), which smooths the points themselves rather than values at them.

Usage

tpsurf(x, y, z, lam = 0, nx = 50L, ny = nx)

# S3 method for class 'tpsurf'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tpsurf'
plot(x, ..., main = NULL, col = NULL, pal = NULL)

Arguments

x, y

The coordinates of the points. For print() and plot(), x is a tpsurf result.

z

The value at each point.

lam

The smoothing: one number from 0 (0 interpolates).

nx, ny

The size of the grid: whole numbers from 2 to 1000.

...

Not used by print(); for plot(), passed to graphics::image().

main

NULL (a default title) or one string.

col

Not used: the surface is shaded by pal.

pal

NULL ("sequential") or a palette name for blpal().

Value

An object of class tpsurf, a list: x and y (the grid), z (the surface on it, nx by ny, as graphics::image() takes it), a (the basis coefficients), beta (const, x, y), fitted, resid and lam. plot() draws the surface with its contours and returns x, y and z invisibly.

Details

The surface is f(s) = sum_i a_i phi(|s - s_i|) + b_0 + b_1 x + b_2 y with the radial basis phi(r) = r^2 log r (Duchon 1977); the coefficients solve the linear system (K + lam I) a + T b = z, T'a = 0, K the basis between the points and T the rows (1, x_i, y_i) (Wahba 1990, ch. 2). The compiled kernel solves it by LU decomposition and evaluates the grid. It refuses points that all lie on one line (the plane is not determined) and, with lam = 0, points that repeat (the system is singular). fitted is the surface at the points, so resid is 0 for lam = 0 up to rounding.

References

Duchon, J. (1977). Splines minimizing rotation-invariant semi-norms in Sobolev spaces. In W. Schempp and K. Zeller (eds.), Constructive Theory of Functions of Several Variables, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 571, 85-100. Springer. doi:10.1007/BFb0086566

Wahba, G. (1990). Spline Models for Observational Data. SIAM. doi:10.1137/1.9781611970128

Examples

set.seed(2)
x <- runif(40)
y <- runif(40)
s <- tpsurf(x, y, sin(4 * x) + y^2 + rnorm(40, sd = 0.05), lam = 0.001,
            nx = 30)
s
#> tpsurf: thin-plate spline of 40 points, lambda 0.001, residual sum of squares 0.002046; grid 30 x 30
plot(s)
